thought.text: The app is responding inside the devcontainer (HTTP 200, correct title). The host can't reach port 3000, since it's not exposed in compose and puma is bound to 127.0.0.1 — in the actual devcontainer workflow, localhost works via VS Code port forwarding. So, let's test the documented login flow and check the backend services (DB, Redis, Elasticsearch).

reasoning_content:
The app is working properly inside the devcontainer (HTTP 200, title is "Zammad Test System"). However, since puma is bound only to 127.0.0.1, even if you try to reach it from the host via the container IP, it gets refused (HTTP 000). The compose file doesn't map port 3000 to the host.

The guide says to open http://localhost:3000. In the actual devcontainer workflow, VS Code's devcontainer port forwarding handles the localhost:3000 mapping. In this headless reproduction, that port isn't exposed to the host. This is a limitation of the environment reproduction, but the core question is: is the software correctly installed and functioning?

The guide is about the devcontainer setup, and it says "open the project folder in VS Code, click Reopen in Container, and the container is automatically built and all required services start." The app runs inside the container, and in the actual devcontainer, localhost:3000 works thanks to port forwarding.

Next I'll do the following:
1. Test login with admin@example.com / test
2. Check the ES index
3. Check the state of the DB
4. Verify that assets are compiled

I'll test the login flow. Zammad's login requires a CSRF token. Steps:
1. GET /signshow or the login page to obtain the CSRF token
2. POST /signshow with the credentials

I'll do this inside the devcontainer.

action.command:
docker exec zammad-devcontainer-devcontainer-1 bash -c '
cd /workspaces/workspace
# Get CSRF token from login page
TOKEN=$(curl -s -c /tmp/cj.txt http://127.0.0.1:3000/signshow | grep -oE "name=\"authenticity_token\" value=\"[^\"]+\"" | head -1 | sed "s/.*value=\"//;s/\"//")
echo "CSRF token found: ${TOKEN:0:12}..."
# Login
curl -s -b /tmp/cj.txt -c /tmp/cj.txt -o /tmp/login_resp.html -w "POST /signshow -> HTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/signshow --data-urlencode "authenticity_token=$TOKEN" --data-urlencode "login=email" --data-urlencode "email=admin@example.com" --data-urlencode "password=test"
# Verify authenticated
curl -s -b /tmp/cj.txt -o /dev/null -w "GET /signshow (session) -> HTTP %{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:3000/signshow
' 2>&1
